newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria rounds up officials for graft before vote.
newsitem.headline: Algeria rounds up officials for graft before vote.

text.p: Algerian authorities issued a laundry list of charges and jail sentences on officials in state-owned companies in a crackdown on graft ahead of the June 5 general elections.

Eight officials, including the head of a petrol distribution station in the southern town of Laghouat, were sentenced for up to 10 years in jail, said the official Algerian news agency APS, quoting court statements released on Tuesday night.
Among the officials found guilty of corruption was an income tax collector who was sentenced to seven years in prison by a criminal court in the eastern town of Karimia, APS said.
Judges ordered 11 officials, including two in charge of regional cement sales, be held in custody pending trial for embezzlement or acting as middle men in corruption-related affairs, it added.
Algerian opposition politicians and ordinary people blame corruption as a main factor in distrust between the Algeria's 29 million people and the authorities.

Political sources said corruption would be among main themes of the parliamentary election campaign beginning in mid-May. About 8,000 candidates are standing for the 380-seat National Assembly elections under the banners of some 40 parties or as independent contenders.
Algeria has been without an elected parliament since 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election in which radical Islamists had taken a commanding lead.
About 60,000 people have died since then in violence pitting Moslem guerrillas against government forces.
